body:
The below MRP confirms that rotated() rotates the vector CCW when looking against the axis. I think it would be best to term it this way as thats the standard convention in maths textbooks (e.g. vector calculus, or the standard 3x3 rotation matrices in 3D), and it also coincides with what the docs currently have (e.g. in Basis.xml line 253, or Transform3D.xml line 122).

https://github.com/BenBlueeeee/godot-vector3-rotation-direction

e.g. this wiki page uses this convention https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotation_matrix#In_three_dimensions

> The below MRP confirms that rotated() rotates the vector CCW when looking against the axis. 

That'd be the ["right hand rule"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right-hand_rule#A_rotating_body)

So should we word it something like this for 3D?

> The [param axis] must be a normalized vector (see [method Vector3.normalized]). If [param angle] is positive, the basis is rotated counter-clockwise around the axis according to the right hand rule.

It also might be worth double checking whether it's clockwise in 2D (like the current wording suggests).

There is also another slightly longer winded wording here https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_vector3.html#class-vector3-method-signed-angle-to

> [float](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_float.html#class-float) signed_angle_to(to: [Vector3](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_vector3.html#class-vector3), axis: [Vector3](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_vector3.html#class-vector3)) const
> 
> Returns the signed angle to the given vector, in radians. The sign of the angle is positive in a counter-clockwise direction and negative in a clockwise direction when viewed from the side specified by the axis.

which might be worth aligning to whichever wording we decide upon.

I think the options are

- ... counter_clockwise when viewed along the direction antiparallel to the given axis
- ... counter_clockwise when looking against the given axis
- ... counter_clockwise, according to the right hand rule

Personally I would vote for the 1st one.

> ... counter_clockwise when looking against the given axis

I went with this, as it's likely the most intuitive for people coming from less math-intensive backgrounds.

It seems like the issue is the most intuitive statement for people who don't have a maths background would be "CW when looking along", but for people with a maths background the most common wording is "CCW when looking against".

So there will probably never be a one size fits all solution here; its just a matter of deciding whether to go with an (arguably unclear) convention that already exists, or create a new one.
We don't have any uses of "against" and a lot of uses of "along" for these, so I don't think it makes sense to break with convention as a new exception

Quaternion also has an initialiser that specifies an angle around an axis, might worth adding in the wording there too:

https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_quaternion.html#class-quaternion-constructor-quaternion:~:text=Quaternion%20Quaternion%28axis%3A%20Vector3%2C%20angle%3A%20float%29

Throwing another opinion into the mix (I have a heavily mathematical background):

## Looking against the axis

> e.g. this wiki page uses this convention https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotation_matrix#In_three_dimensions

I'm just going to point there are no matches for the word "against" anywhere on that wiki page. The convention they seem to use now is:

> a rotation about one of the axes

## Looking along the axis

> It seems like the issue is the most intuitive statement for people who don't have a maths background would be "CW when looking along", but for people with a maths background the most common wording is "CCW when looking against".

I will reiterate, I have a very mathematical background, pure/abstract mathematics to be precise. I still find "looking along" clearer than "looking against". So I would argue that even for maths backgrounds, this opinion is debatable.

> We don't have any uses of "against" and a lot of uses of "along" for these, so I don't think it makes sense to break with convention as a new exception

I also agree with not rocking the boat more than necessary.

## Around the axis

The axes are displayed as lines, in a 3D space I can immediately visualise what it means to _rotate around it_.

 I would also point out that the Blender docs use this phrase as well:

> Rotation involves changing the orientation of elements around one or more axes or the Pivot Point.
[Rotate - Blender Docs](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/scene_layout/object/editing/transform/rotate.html#rotate)

I have no basis for the following claim (other than both programs being FOSS) but I would expect most people making 3D games in Godot, make 3D models in Blender. 

So, if it were up to me, I would stick with "around" (then using "along" where necessary).

After thinking about it a bit more, I fully agree that the looking-along convention is best. However, I just want to write some thoughts to clarify why.

---

### Convention

Keeping with convention has been mentioned a couple of times, so I thought I would summarise what conventions are currently used in Godot when talking about rotations. In 3D, the looking along convention is equivalent to saying CW-positive. (I will just use CW-positive & CCW-positive for simplicity).

- CCW-positive is used by:
    - The 3D classes Vector3, Basis, Transform3D
    - Input's get_joy_gyroscope()
- CW positive is used by:
    - All of 2D
    - Curve3D (uses the phrase "along" an axis)
    - Using transforms tutorial page

Curve3D was the only example of a 3D class using CW-positive for a rotation axis that I could find.

---

### Why use CW-positive

- [This page](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/math/matrices_and_transforms.html) says that rotations are defined clockwise in Godot (aka, CW-positive) - and because Godot uses left-handed in 3D this cancels-out. Obviously, if we want this page to be accurate, everything should be defined CW-positive.

- Since godot is left-handed, if we want 3D rotations to be defined analagously to 2D, we should define them CW-positive (in 2D, you are effectively looking _along_ the +z axis)

- Everyone here prefers CW-positive

---

I am just trying to point out that currently, major 3D classes do use CCW-positive. Changing to CW-positive directly breaks the convention in Vector3, Basis, and Transform3D. (It's just that the direction used is implicit and so no mention of the "against" appears.) Despite this I think CW-positive is best.

However, since the use of the word "around" in these 3 classes currently means when looking against the axis, I think solely saying "CW around" would be confusing. @charjr interprets "around" as being facing along the axis, but the original author of those class pages interpreted "around" as meaning the opposite.

Clearly, both conventions exist and are used, so explicitly using "along" everywhere is simpler and prevents any confusions.

---

It seems like everyone prefers CW-positive instead of CCW-positive, so I vote to go with that. As long as its consistent everywhere, it doesn't really matter.

This post is sort of a debate against myself, but I think its good to document why we are changing this, in case someone in the future disagrees or restarts a discussion.
